title: Flexion-relaxation
summary: Simulate static forward flexion and report back-muscle activation (%MVC) at each angle, and the angles where back-muscle activity stops and resumes.
simulate: Scale the model to the study subject (table below).
Impose the static posture at the task's flexion angle (check angle_def); knees straight.
Apply the hand load (none, 10 or 14 kg, arms hanging).
Report activation under each electrode, normalised as the study did (emg_ref).
FR angle tasks: report the angle where back-muscle activity drops to ~0 (onset) and returns (cessation).

ghezelbash2020.note: weighted means; F 163.4 cm 61.0 kg, M 174.6 cm 72.2 kg

notes: Angle definitions differ (trunk flexion, trunk inclination, lumbar T12-S1, Gupta thigh-T1); each task states it. Ghezelbash 2020 load heights mapped to angles from Ghezelbash 2024 Fig 3c.
EMG references differ: max over 6 MVEs (Ghezelbash), angle-specific MVC (Shin), supine MVC (Koopman, medians). Normalise model activity the same way.

Left out: passive moments (Dolan 1994, Zwambag 2016/2020: not EMG), FR ratio (Descarreaux), EMG timing in % cycle (Olson 2006), EMG at full flexion without angle (Toussaint 1995). More conditions in raw tests.
agent_prompt: You are validating a trunk musculoskeletal model against flexion-relaxation data. For each task, scale the model to the study subject in `subjects`, impose the static forward-flexion posture given by flexion_deg (respect angle_def), apply the hand load, and solve for muscle activation. Report activation (%) of the muscles under the named electrode site, normalised like the study (emg_ref: max over six maximal exertions, angle-specific maximal extension, or supine MVC). For FR angle tasks (output fr_angle), sweep flexion in 1-deg steps and report the angle where back-muscle activity first falls to near zero (onset, flexing) or reappears (cessation, extending). Do not tune the model to these data. Return one JSON object following answer_format: task id -> {output key: value}.
